question_text: Determine the density of BCC iron, which has a lattice parameter of 0.2866 nm. The atomic mass of iron is 55.847 g/mol, and the Avogadro constant is $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ atoms/mol. The volume of the unit cell can be calculated using the formula $V = a_{0}^{3}$, where $a_{0}$ is the lattice parameter. The theoretical density can be calculated using the formula $\rho = \frac{(\text{number of atoms/cell})(\text{atomic mass})}{(\text{volume of unit cell})(\text{Avogadro constant})}$.The unit of the answer is g/cm^3.
response:
For BCC iron, there are **2 atoms per unit cell**. Converting the lattice parameter to cm: $a_0 = 0.2866\,\text{nm} = 2.866\times10^{-8}\,\text{cm}$.

$$V = a_0^3 = (2.866\times10^{-8})^3 = 2.356\times10^{-23}\,\text{cm}^3$$

$$\rho = \frac{(2)(55.847)}{(2.356\times10^{-23})(6.022\times10^{23})} \approx 7.88\,\text{g/cm}^3$$

$$\boxed{7.88}$$
